html:
The Berbice Rebellion was a revolt of enslaved Africans in the Dutch colony of Berbice, in what is now Guyana, that began on 23 February 1763 and held much of the colony for about a year.

Disease and hunger had weakened the planters, and the enslaved rose on the plantations along the Canje and Berbice rivers. Led by Coffy, a man born in West Africa, they drove the Dutch to the coast and tried to rule the colony themselves. Quarrels split the rebel leaders, and Dutch troops with help from neighbouring colonies and Indigenous allies crushed the revolt.

Guyana celebrates its Republic Day on 23 February, and the 1763 Monument in Georgetown shows Coffy. It is remembered with later revolts such as the Demerara rebellion as part of the struggle against the Atlantic slave system in Guyana.
sum: The Berbice Rebellion was a revolt of enslaved Africans in the Dutch colony of Berbice, in what is now Guyana, that began on 23 February 1763 and held much of the colony for about a year.
